speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Could you tell me your age, and have you noticed any unusual bleeding from your gums or nose along with the bruising? Also, has the leg pain been constant, or does it come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing generalized fatigue and easy bruising for 3 weeks. Over the past week, she has developed a fever and severe leg pain that wakes her up at night.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any swelling or redness around the painful leg joints, and has she been losing weight recently? Also, has anyone in her family been diagnosed with blood disorders or cancer?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and easy bruising. I also have Fever, Severe leg pain that disturbs sleep.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to know if she has any swollen lymph nodes, particularly in the neck, armpits, or groin. Additionally, does the leg pain seem to be centered in the bones themselves rather than the joints?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable past medical history. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one younger sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with differential and peripheral smear. Do you feel the leg pain is localized to specific bones, and have you noticed any lumps in her neck, armpits, or groin?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: Hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL; Leukocyte Count 63,000/mm3 (elevated); Platelet Count 27,000/mm3 (decreased). Bone Marrow Aspirate: Predominantly immature cells positive for CD10, CD19, and TdT. Vital Signs: Temperature 38.3°C, Heart Rate 120/min, Respiratory Rate 30/min. General Exam: Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy detected; Liver palpable 3 cm below right costal margin; Spleen palpable 2 cm below left costal margin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results confirm acute lymphoblastic leukemia, so I have all the information needed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL).
